title: The serpent vocabulary as faction memory
statement: The Hebrew Bible's serpentine vocabulary cluster — nachash in Genesis 3, the tannin and liwyatan of the prophetic and poetic passages — is read as the memory vocabulary through which the tradition preserves the exiled creator faction: the disclosing figure of Eden and the pursued exiles of the conflict, with the chaos-serpent and wisdom-serpent strands kept distinct; structural convergence with independent modern readings is registered without resting on any etymology, failed etymologies being explicitly severed from the case.

includes: The vocabulary cluster and its distribution: nachash (Genesis 3; Isaiah 27:1), tannin, liwyatan — with the chaos-serpent and wisdom-serpent strands distinguished as the corpus's iconographic work (against Black & Green's verified entries) requires
The referent reading: the cluster as transformed memory of the Serpentine faction within the conflict recorded as woh-claim-0008

The methodological discipline the Archdeacon Explainer models: structural convergence between independent readers of the same texts is registered as convergence, and any case resting on a failed etymology is cut loose rather than defended
excludes: Etymological arguments connecting serpent vocabulary to the faction; the record asserts referential memory, never derivation
Uniform reference across every serpent occurrence; inclusion is per-passage editorial work
The Ugaritic transmission of the Litan formula as a framework claim; the documented cognate is philology's (recorded in the woh-claim-0004 apparatus) and is not contested
Zoological or symbolic readings as targets; the record engages the scholarly accounts, not straw versions

source_references.locator: Chapter 2 (the serpent faction, the disclosure, the exile; the dragons material at the Truth chapter's paragraph 22 as the Explainer locates it)
Isaiah 27:1 (liwyatan, the fleeing and twisting serpent, the tannin in the sea)
The chaos-dragon and wisdom-serpent iconography entries the corpus uses to keep the two strands distinct (verified excerpt; see the source note)
The independent modern reading whose structural convergence the Archdeacon Explainer registers — and whose etymological missteps it severs from the case

alternatives.statement: The tannin/liwyatan passages are inherited chaoskampf theology (Gunkel; Day); the vocabulary preserves Canaanite myth, not any faction.
The Genesis nachash is a wisdom-and-cunning figure within the garden aetiology; symbol, not referent.
Independent readers converging on 'plural powerful ones' reflects the texts' surface features plus a shared modern idiom, not a shared correct referent.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0001 or woh-claim-0008 is revised or retired.
Source-language review changes the cited passage observations.
The chaos/wisdom strand distinction fails against further iconographic verification.
Public prose begins resting the case on etymology, which this record excludes.
